baseline.name: Linear-search LRU list
baseline.approach: Scan cached nodes for each key, then move a found node or evict the oldest.
baseline.time: O(c) get/put for c cached items

archived.name: Direct key lookup plus recency list

why: The key table removes the lookup scan, while doubly linked nodes support constant-time recency moves and eviction.
quantitative_comparison: A baseline lookup can inspect c nodes; the archive uses one direct table access and a bounded number of pointer updates. It additionally initializes 10005 table slots; no elapsed-time speedup is measured.
tradeoffs: Keys must fit the fixed domain, and table memory/init cost may be wasteful for sparse or tiny caches. Allocations and key bounds are unchecked.
evidence_basis: Static operation/storage analysis of the exact direct-index implementation; no benchmark.
